newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 7.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
** India's oil pool deficit likely to balloon to 155 billion rupees, petroleum minister T.R. Balu says, fuelling expectations of a fresh hike in petroleum prices.
** The income tax department conducts nationwide raids on premises of former federal ministers in connection with allegations of illegal foreign exchange transactions.
** Former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao gets temporary relief in the form of bail in a $100,000 cheating case.
** India decides to establish a cell to monitor inflow of foreign direct investment in projects where the investment approvals are at 1.0 billion rupees and above.
** The Indian rupee INR= opened steady at 35.72/73 per dollar. Dollar seen trading at a 35.71/75 range.
** Indian blue-chip shares drifted lower on Wednesday, dragged down by scandal-hit ITC stock.
** The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange index .BSESN fell 18.68 points to 3,044.1.
** ITC crashed 24.75 rupees or 9.2 percent to close at 244.0 rupees on the BSE.
** The Delhi share index dropped 0.75 points to 692.20.

** Officials of B.A.T. Industries Plc, who held talks with financial institutions on Tuesday, will hold another crucial meeting early next week ahead of a special board meeting of ITC. B.A.T. seen keen on introducing "fresh blood" on the ITC board.
** The boards of Raymond Ltd and Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd meeting on Thursday to consider unaudited results for the first half of 1996/97 (April-March).
